text:
maya: Quick question — how does our notify routing stack resolve when multiple SLO alerts fire for the same service? e.g., tenant-level SLO breach + global SLO + per-route notify. Console today isn't super explicit about which channel wins. Need to make this clearer for rollout docs and oncall expectations.

sam: Short answer: the notify service evaluates a policy_stack (ordered). explicit per-route policies take precedence, then tenant defaults, then org/global defaults. But the console currently only shows the active policy, not the full precedence chain.

devon: Oncall perspective: we keep getting double pings when tenant + global both target pagerduty. Dedupe is best-effort and sometimes fails (different integrations). We should avoid blind fanout expansion during rollouts.

maya: Could we surface a "predicted routing" preview in the SLO editor? Something lightweight: Trigger -> Primary channel -> Fallbacks -> quota behavior. That would help SOs understand impact before enabling.

kelly: UX note: love the preview but keep it compact. Maybe a small inline summary row with a hover or popover for full details. "Preview routing" button that fetches simulation.

toni: Product: Also we need to consider notify quotas. If tenant's notify quota is exhausted we currently fall back to a pooled ops channel — that fallback needs to be visible in the preview and flagged as a cost/SL impact.

sam: Implementation detail: notify-service currently stores policy_stacks as an ordered array. Dedupe runs on fingerprint/hash of (alert_id, service_id) but different integrations (PD vs Slack) have different fingerprints so duplicates slip through. We can: 1) add a canonical dedupe layer, 2) expose the evaluation order to the console, and 3) add a per-tenant suppression TTL.

maya: Could we offer an API for previewing routing so the console doesn't have to replicate the logic? e.g. POST /v1/notify/preview with a minimal payload and we return predicted channels + reasons.

sam: Yeah, here's a minimal example we can implement quickly:
```
POST /v1/notify/preview
{
  "tenant_id": "acct-123",
  "slo_id": "slo-99",
  "event": "breach",
  "timestamp": 1943219999
}
```
Response would include ordered channels, whether quota would trigger fallback, and a TTL suggestion for suppression.

alerts-bot: preview job 98122 created, duration 34ms :white_check_mark:

devon: Telemetry ask: instrument predicted_vs_actual routing so we can surface mismatch rate in rollout dashboards. Label suggestions: preview.routing, notify.sent_channel, notify.fallback_used (bool), notify.dedupe_hit (bool).

sam: Agree — add those labels to notify-emitted events and preview responses. We'll need a migration plan for existing dashboards.

toni: For rollouts UX: block changes that increase global fanout by default during canary unless product owner acknowledges. Show a diff in the editor: before vs after routing set.

kelly: I'll prototype a compact diff UI and a hoverable "why this route" explanation. Will also include an accessibility-friendly table view.

maya: Action items: sam to spec the /v1/notify/preview API + canonical dedupe RFC by EOD; devon to add telemetry labels and a sample dashboard query; kelly to produce mockups by tomorrow.

sam: Will do. Adding spec to #eng-platform RFCs and linking here when ready.

devon: I'll push a telemetry PR to record preview_vs_actual events to the notify stream.

kelly: Mockups incoming, ping me for design review.

maya: Thanks everyone — this should reduce noisy double-pings during canaries. :thumbsup:
